arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case contends Texas rules effectively bar ineffective assistance claims on direct appeal. The state contends its procedures offer generous opportunities to raise these claims.
Justice Alito questioned the practicality of case-by-case determinations in other states. Justice Kennedy asked how the Court should formulate the rule if it favors the side that brought the case.

the side that brought the case cited Texas court statements that direct appeal is not the preferred route. The state argued its procedures provide constitutionally protected opportunities to raise claims.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Martinez rule. It asks if Texas procedures satisfy federal standards for raising ineffective assistance claims.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on February 25, 2013.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to find Texas procedures inadequate. This would allow the ineffective assistance claim to proceed.
The state wants the Court to uphold Texas procedures. This would keep the claim barred from federal review.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues Texas rules make it virtually impossible to raise these claims on direct appeal. This creates a procedural barrier that violates federal rights.
The state argues its procedures are among the most generous in the country. It claims defendants receive two opportunities to raise these claims.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Ginsburg asked if Martinez applies when Texas allows direct appeal but notes transcript limitations.
Chief Justice Roberts asked if the appellate court has ever allowed such claims on direct appeal before.
